question.problem: Given the ellipsoid $\frac{{x}^{2}}{25}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{9}+(z-1)^{2}=1$, find the domain of $z=z(x,y).$
question.worked_solution:
From the ellipsoid equation, we make $z$ the subject as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}}{25}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{9}+(z-1)^{2} & =1 \\ (z-1)^{2} & =1-\frac{{x}^{2}}{25}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{9} \\ z-1 & =\pm \sqrt{1-\frac{{x}^{2}}{25}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{9}}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Since the square root is defined only for non-negative arguments, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}1-\frac{{x}^{2}}{25}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{9}\ge 0 \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{25}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{9}\le 1\end{aligned}
$$

which gives the interior of the ellipse $\frac{{x}^{2}}{25}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{9}=1$ and its boundary.

Therefore, the domain is 

$$
\{(x,y)\,:\,\frac{{x}^{2}}{25}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{9}\le 1\}.
$$
